clue.text: Society man joining elite closer to wine?

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
the elite are the top people

explanation.surface: A society gentleman mingles with the upper crust, perhaps getting cosy with the wine list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' is a thing that closes, not a comparative of close; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw cap is the stopper sealing many modern bottles, so it literally closes the wine.

clue.text: A representative leaving mushroom and bun

indicators.note: leaving says these letters depart from the mushroom word, so they are removed

parts.note: champignon is the French word for a mushroom, used in English for the button kind
MP, a Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A politician walks out on a meal of mushrooms and bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: AMP comes out of the middle of CHAMPIGNON. 'Bun' is the hairstyle, not the bread roll the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A chignon is a knot or coil of hair worn at the back of the head, a kind of hair bun.

clue.text: Film duck eating seconds in Scots town

indicators.note: eating says the duck swallows the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck prized for its down

indicators.note: in places the seconds inside the town's name

parts.note: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland
S is the abbreviation for seconds of time

explanation.surface: A duck tucks into a meal at a Scottish town, consuming seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested insertions: 'in' puts the seconds within the Scots town, and 'eating' has the duck swallow that whole result.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is the 1969 road movie starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper.

clue.text: Host runs out in skimpy knickers

indicators.note: out says the runs are taken away from the host word

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, a throng
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A party host dashes outside wearing nothing but scanty underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' is a multitude here, not someone giving a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a minimal undergarment with a narrow strip at the back, so skimpy briefs.

clue.text: Fierce sort from country seen in pub area

indicators.note: seen in says the country is placed within the pub abbreviation

parts.note: PH, public house, is the abbreviation for a pub
Iran is a country in western Asia

explanation.surface: Someone aggressive from abroad is spotted in the local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fierce sort' sounds like a person; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a South American freshwater fish notorious for its savage, flesh-tearing bite.

clue.text: Shared on line: season almost over

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the line letter follows
over means turned over, so the shortened season is read backwards
almost says the season word loses its last letter

parts.note: autumn is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: Something passed around online as the summer season nears its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On line' looks like 'online', but splits: 'on' sets the line letter alongside. 'Almost' trims the season and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual describes something held in common by two or more parties, as in a mutual friend.

clue.text: When sloshed emerge in a confused crowd

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Drunken revellers stumble out into a bewildered mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals, and by extension any strange, varied, unruly assortment of people.

clue.text: Ecstasy dropped into the wine as principle?

indicators.note: dropped into says the drug letter is slipped inside the wine word

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, once used for communion
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Spiking the wine with ecstasy — is that a matter of principle?
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a rare word for a sweet dark red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a principle someone lives by.

clue.text: Lots here getting something done about upper-class

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the action word goes round the class letter

parts.note: an action is something done, a deed
U is the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Lots of people get things done concerning the posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are the items for sale, not a quantity; U-and-non-U is the old British upper-class label.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are numbered items put up for sale, and they are bid for at an auction house.

clue.text: Conservative in Sofia spinning debacle

indicators.note: in places the Conservative letter within the spun city name
spinning rotates the city name, moving letters from its front to its back

explanation.surface: A Tory politician on a turbulent trip to the Bulgarian capital ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' moves SO from the front of SOFIA to the end, giving FIASO; C goes in before the last O.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete debacle.

clue.text: Interim football manager called 'The Devil'

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called
Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil

explanation.surface: A caretaker coach nicknamed after Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralf Rangnick was Manchester United's interim manager in 2021-22.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralf Rangnick, the German coach, took temporary charge of Manchester United after Solskjaer's sacking.

clue.text: No information, doctor admitted, on a hormone

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the rest follows the article
admitted means let in, so the doctor goes inside the word no

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A doctor checked in but admitted knowing nothing about a hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No information' looks like one idea but splits into two pieces, with 'admitted' placing the doctor inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Androgens such as testosterone are steroid hormones that control male characteristics.

clue.text: Go-slow endless in grotesque style

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless says the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: thick means slow-witted, dim

explanation.surface: An industrial go-slow turns into something bizarre and unending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go-slow' looks like one word, the industrial action, but splits into GO and 'slow' (thick, as in dim).
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic fiction and design favour the macabre, the gloomy and the grotesque.

clue.text: Camelot woman some drunken idiot

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lady at King Arthur's court is a bit of a drunken fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is the wife of Geraint in the Arthurian tales, a lady of Arthur's court.

clue.text: Rutland fossil reanimated so a danger

indicators.note: reanimated means brought back to life in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fossil from England's smallest county is brought back to life, posing a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rutland is England's smallest county; its reservoir yielded a huge ichthyosaur skeleton in 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rutland sea dragon is the nickname of an ichthyosaur fossil found at Rutland Water.

clue.text: Instruction from shooter perhaps at Caerphilly?

parts.note: say means for example, perhaps
Caerphilly is a crumbly white Welsh cheese

explanation.surface: A gunman issuing orders in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' is a photographer, not a gunman; Caerphilly is both a town and a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers tell their subjects to say this so their mouths form a smile for the picture.

clue.text: Sozzled, sneak swig showing lack of coordination

indicators.note: sozzled means very drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk who sneaks a swig shows how badly co-ordinated they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawkiness is awkwardness and clumsiness of movement, a failure of physical coordination.

clue.text: Scandal: Tories for example shown exit?

parts.note: the Conservatives are an example of a political party
a gate is a way out

explanation.surface: A scandal: Conservatives, say, are shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Partygate was the scandal over lockdown parties in Downing Street in 2020-21.
explanation.definitionFit: Partygate was the political scandal over gatherings held in Downing Street during Covid lockdowns.

clue.text: Vulgarian censure overturned? Say pub closed early

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the censure word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke, censure

indicators.note: closed early means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a pub is an example of a venue

explanation.surface: A boor's ban is lifted, perhaps because the pub shut early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' turns RAP into PAR; 'Say pub' is VENUE, cut short to VENU.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart newly rich person who lacks refinement, a vulgarian.

clue.text: Astonishing answer on issue about unknown elected

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed on top, so this letter comes first
about means surrounding, so the issue word goes round the others

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a mag
Z is a mathematical unknown
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A surprising reply about a matter involving an elected stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is a magazine number, not a matter for debate; 'about' wraps it round the unknown and the elected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amazing causes great surprise or wonder, so it is astonishing.

clue.text: See 21
16 Across investigator argues poorly: Tory ultimately supporting

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed beneath the rest
poorly means badly done, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Partygate investigator argues badly, with a Tory backing her in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: SUEGRA comes from rearranging ARGUES; the last letter of 'Tory' goes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue Gray, the senior civil servant, led the official inquiry into the Partygate gatherings.

clue.text: Sunak needing this short article on good argument

indicators.note: on in an across clue means attached after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a row is a quarrel, an argument

indicators.note: short means the article word loses its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister needs a brief item on a good row.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister 2022-24 and constantly promised economic expansion; 'short' trims the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi Sunak, as Prime Minister, kept saying the economy needed this expansion.

clue.text: With partying, what was guzzled? Conceal disreputable affair

definitions.meaning: ... wine and other ..., slang for drink, were swilled at the parties

explanation.surface: A question about what was drunk at the Downing Street parties, then the cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is playful: white (wine) plus wash, an old word for liquor or swill.
explanation.definitionFit: To whitewash wrongdoing is to gloss over it and hide the facts from scrutiny.

clue.text: Attacked: enjoyed festive booze-up without wife

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the wife letter is removed

parts.note: to wassail is to drink and make merry at Christmas

explanation.surface: Assaulted after a Christmas drinking binge, minus the wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assailed is to be set upon violently, physically or verbally attacked.

clue.text: Bones in bag next to top drawer?

indicators.note: next to means the pieces sit side by side in the answer

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
an RA, a Royal Academician, is a leading artist, so a top drawer

explanation.surface: Bones kept in a bag beside the best chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is someone who draws, not furniture; a Royal Academician is a top one.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacra are plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Drink one to limit bone disease

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose, so the drink word surrounds the bone

parts.note: beer is a drink
a rib is a bone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Have one drink to stave off bone disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To limit' reads like purpose in the surface, but signals the drink enclosing the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by deficiency of thiamine, vitamin B1.

clue.text: Church empties, vacated, Queen brought in? Here's to it!

indicators.note: brought in means the Queen letters are placed inside
vacated means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The church clears out its empty bottles and the Queen raises a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empties' sounds like returned bottles; here 'vacated' strips the word to its outer letters and 'brought in' inserts the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is said when raising a glass, the same toast as here's to it.

clue.text: Mrs Jack Brooksbank not one for Ionesco?

indicators.note: not one means the numeral letter is left out

parts.note: Princess Eugenie is married to Jack Brooksbank
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Is Princess Eugenie not suited to a role in an absurdist play?
explanation.walkthrough: Eugenie is a British princess, granddaughter of Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was the Romanian-French playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Artificial organ composer Tees heard

parts.note: Philip Glass is a minimalist composer

indicators.note: heard means the setter's pronoun is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Tees is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: An artificial organ attributed to composer Tees, as overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Tees calls himself I, which said out loud is EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass eye is a prosthesis replacing a lost eye, one of the body's sensory parts.
